description: Concatenation expression - the & operator joining literals (§2023:8.8.3) - a COBOL-2002 introduction (roadmap D6; the 2023 CONCAT function is defined by reference to this operator). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): ANSI X3.23-1985 has no concatenation operator: its operators are arithmetic, §1985:VI.6.2.2: "There are five binary arithmetic operators and two unary arithmetic operators that may be used in arithmetic expressions", and a literal is one delimited string, §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1: "A nonnumeric literal is a character-string delimited at the beginning and at the end by the separator quotation mark"; §2002:F.1 item 6 ("The following reserved words have been added") lists `&`. §2002:8.7.3 adds "The concatenation operator is the COBOL character '&', which shall be immediately preceded and followed by a separator space" and §2002:8.8.3 "A concatenation expression consists of two operands separated by the concatenation operator", and §2002:F.2 item 31 states the change: "A concatenation expression operates on two literals of the same class to concatenate their values." §2014:8.8.3 and §2023:8.8.3 carry the 2002 sentence unchanged. ACTIVE as of P10 Step 14: a compile-time fold to the equivalent single literal (§2023:8.8.3.3 GR3) via ConcatFolder; the §2023:8.8.3.2 SRs are COBOL1540/1541/1545; the introduction gate is the VersionConformancePass parse arm (VisitConcatenationExpression).
